GABA-mediated random fluctuations in Cl(-) channel activity are a normal property of embryonic hippocampal neurons in culture.
Cl- channel activity fluctuates spontaneously in cultured embryonic hippocampal neurons and is mediated by tonic secretion of GABA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of GABAergic inhibitory synapses in the rat CNS.
the mechanisms of GABAergic neurotransmission in the developing rat hippocampus.
the development of a model of the GABAergic system that is based on the hypothesis that the GABAergic synapse is a specialized form of the GABA-Cl(-)-secretory system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cl(-)-dependent GABAergic signal in the rat hippocampus is not a transient but rather a fluctuating baseline.
GABA is secreted in the embryonic hippocampus in both tonic and transient modes.
the Cl- conductance in the hippocampus is tonically activated by GABA in the embryo, and by GABA and by glutamate in the adult.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAergic system is a dynamic system in which GABA is secreted continuously and tonically, and in which GABA-mediated transients are superimposed on this tonic background.

GABA secretion is a continuous process, not an all or none event, that GABA secretion may be regulated by the frequency, not only by the amount, of GABA secreted and that GABA secretion can be modulated by GABA.
the embryonic CNS is a Cl(-)-dependent GABAergic milieu in which GABA is continuously secreted and randomly activates Cl- channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GABAergic system is more complex than previously appreciated and that GABA can act on neurons in a variety of ways, including as a neurotransmitter and a neuromodulator.
GABA-mediated Cl- conductances can be either transient or steady-state.
GABA secretion and Cl- conductances in cultured hippocampal neurons are not restricted to synaptic events.
